The uncontrolled dendrite growth and detrimental parasitic reactions of Zn
anodes currently impede the large-scale implementation of aqueous zinc ion
batteries. Here, we design a versatile quasi-solid-state polymer electrolyte with
highly selective ion transport channels via molecular crosslinking of sodium
polyacrylate, lithium magnesium silicate and cellulose nanoﬁber. The abun-
dant negatively charged ionic channels modulate Zn2+ desolvation process and
facilitate ion transport. Moreover, an in-situ formed Zn-Mg-Si medium-entropy
alloy on Zn anode allows for an improved Zn nucleation kinetics and homo-
geneous Zn deposition. These combined advantages of the polymer electro-
lyte enable Zn anodes to achieve an average Coulombic efﬁciency of 99.7 %
over 2400 cycles and highly reversible cycling up to 600 h with large depth of
discharge of 85.6%. The resultant Zn | |V2O5 offers a stable long-term cycling
performance and its pouch cell achieves a cycling capacity of 1.13 Ah at
industrial-level loading mass of 31.3 mg.
Aqueous zinc ion batteries (AZIBs) have emerged as a prospective
alternative for energy storage systems in the “post-lithium” era, due to
their advantageous characteristics of high safety, cost-effectiveness
and environmentally benignity1,2. However, AZIBs still face the sig-
niﬁcant challenges, such as the accretion of inactive by-product on the
surface of Zn anodes because of excessive free water and subsequent
side reactions. This dramatically deteriorate the issues related to local
chemical corrosion, passivation, and hydrogen evolution, resulting in
low Coulombic efﬁciency (CE) and irreversible Zn loss. More press-
ingly, the boom of intractable Zn dendrites initiated by the limited
nucleation sites and heterogeneous Zn plating are prone to puncture
the separator during repeated electrochemical testing and cause per-
manent device failure, posing a critical obstacle to the practical
application of highly stable AZIBs3,4. Thereout, it is imperative to open
up efﬁcient pathways to fundamentally conquer the challenges of
dendrite growth and internal short circuits.
Quasi-solid-state polymer electrolytes (QSPEs) as a promising
kind of “beyond aqueous” electrolytes that reconcile mechanical
properties of solid electrolytes and ionic diffusion behaviors of liquid
electrolytes are triggered to break through the aforesaid obstacles in
AZIBs. Since QSPEs can avoid liquid leakage with high ﬂexible and
elasticity of polymer matrices, they are helpful to stabilize solid-

vinyl alcohol7, polyacrylamide8, and polysaccharide9, have been
employed for the preparation of QSPEs. However, they often
encounter the cruxes of low ionic conductivity and high interfacial
impedance due to less water content. To address these problems, the
incorporation of molecular-level designed microchannels within
QSPEs, which could regulate solvation structure of Zn2+ ions and pro-
mote ion transport behavior to enhance Zn2+ deposition kinetics, has
been identiﬁed as an efﬁcient approach10. In response, researches have
reported that the polymer networks with charged anionic or cationic
groups possess a unique zincophilic ability, allowing for homogenized
ion distributions and three-dimensional (3D) diffusion mechanism on
Zn anode11,12. In addition, the charged groups (e.g., carboxyl, sulfonate,
phosphate and hydroxyl groups) inherently contribute to a ﬁrm
adherence between substrate and polymer electrolyte, which in turn
restrains interfacial dislocation and maintains stable electrode reac-
tions. Unfortunately, establishing Zn2+ ion migration channels in the
polymer networks comes with a downside - it reduces the selectivity of
ions, resulting in high voltage hysteresis and the formation of by-
product8. The challenge lies in reconciling the conﬂicting require-
ments of ion sieving and migration in QSPEs. When Zn ions inﬁltrate
the polymer electrolytes, they can interact with the charged groups,
altering the original hydrogen-bond networks. This leads to an
increase in free water content and water activity, weakening water
retention and even compromising electrode stabilities. Additionally,
achieving a balance between mechanical properties and ionic con-
ductivity of QSPEs is difﬁcult. Because strong mechanical properties
rely on high polymer crystallinity, whereas high ionic migration and
conductivity necessitate amorphous and loosely-structured micro-
environments within the polymer networks13. Thus, there is an urgent
need to enhance both ionic conductivity and selectivity, while main-
taining mechanical strength, to enable high-performance AZIBs.
Here, to cope with these above-mentioned challenges, we
designed a versatile QSPE with rapid Zn-ion diffusion, high selectivity
and strong mechanical properties through the cross-linking of
sodium polyacrylate (PAAS), lithium magnesium silicate (LMS) and
cellulose nanoﬁber (CNF). PAAS and LMS were ﬁrst dissolved in CNF
solution to establish physical entanglement and after dried, followed
by complete Zn2+ ion exchange in ZnSO4 solution. The prepared
polymer electrolyte is designated as PLCZ. For comparative pur-
poses, we also prepared a polymer electrolyte without the LMS
additive (PCZ) and an aqueous ZnSO4 electrolyte equipped with a
CNF separator (CZ). The LMS platelets, consisting of silicate tetra-
hedrons and intermediate octahedrons of Li and Mg ions coordi-
nated with oxygen atoms and hydroxyl groups, create an anisotropic
charge distribution where the silicate tetrahedron layers induce a
negative charge and Mg-O octahedrons in the platelet edge have
positive charge (Supplementary Fig. S1)14,15. Therefore, the Mg-O
octahedrons allow for easy bonding with the carboxylate (-COO-)
groups in polymer chain via electrostatic interaction, orchestrating
the assembly of microchannels constituted by -COO- groups and
silicate tetrahedrons (Fig. 1a). Then, by selectively gathering Zn2+ ions
in the created microchannels through LMS and PAAS, ion migration
in and out of the PLCZ electrolyte can be rapidly forced by con-
centration gradients and electric ﬁelds. The constructed ion migra-
tion channels effectively modulate Zn2+ solvation structure and repel
SO4
2- anions, thus relieving by-product generation. Excitingly, a
compact and ﬁrm SEI protection of Zn-Mg-Si medium-entropy alloy
(MEA) is in-situ made through the co-reduction of LMS and Zn2+ ions.
The resultant MEA SEI owns ultrahigh Young’s modulus (11.07 GPa)
and brilliant zincophilic afﬁnity, bringing uniform Zn deposition of
(002) planes and effective dendrite suppression. The superb features
of the PLCZ enable Zn | |Zn and Zn | |V2O5 batteries to exhibit highly
stable cycling performances.
Results
Electrolyte structures and properties
The abundant presence of -COO- favors PAAS polymer chains to readily
form hydrogen bonding bridges or electrostatic interactions with
diverse molecules (such as H2O, cellulose, polyvinyl alcohol, metal
cations, etc.). Building upon this understanding, this work employs a
rational design based on molecular engineering utilizing various con-
stituents for the creation of a versatile QSPE with ion-sieving cap-
abilities. As depicted in Supplementary Fig. S2a, the synthesis of the
PLCZ polymer electrolytes involved the blending of PAAS and LMS in a
cellulose dispersion solution, followed by Zn2+ ion exchange proce-
dure, facilitating the formation of a well-connected cross-linked
molecular network. The -COO- groups in PAAS can establish physical
connection with cellulose nanoﬁber matrix (Supplementary Fig. S2b).
Furthermore, owing to the positive charge induced by Mg-O octahe-
dron in the edge of LMS, the larger number of -COO- negative charges
in PAAS chain also provide opportunity to cohere with LMS sheets via
electrostatic interactions (Supplementary Fig. S2c)15,16. Afterwards, the
resulting PAAS-LMS-CNF membrane (Supplementary Fig. S3) was
immersed in ZnSO4 solution to ensure sufﬁcient ion exchange. The
negative charge of -COO- can facilitate the permeation of Zn2+ ion by
metal coordination bonds and concentration gradients, which thus
speeds up Zn2+ diffusion in the PLCZ electrolyte and more importantly,
restructure the solvation structure of hydrated Zn2+ by substituting
partial water molecules (Fig. 1a and Supplementary Fig. S2d)17. On the
other hand, the outer negative charges on the LMS platelet surface
result in the selective adsorption of Zn2+ ion into the interparticle
nanogaps of LMS platelets18,19. Such unique selective aggregation of
Zn2+ ion confers upon LMS platelets and PAAS chains the ability to
work as “ion transfer pumps”, which in turn renders a fast ion trans-
portation, even ion nucleation and homogeneous Zn deposition dur-
ing Zn plating/stripping
process20,21. Molecular dynamics (MD)
simulations were conducted to validate the above inferences (Fig. 1b
and Supplementary Fig. S4). The radial distribution function (RDF) of
the CZ liquid electrolyte reveals a prominent peak of Zn2+-O (H2O) at
2.75 Å, with the coordination number (CN) of 6.06, indicative of the
typical Zn2+ solvation sheath structure ([Zn(H2O)6]2+) in the liquid
solution22. However, the PCZ and PLCZ electrolytes exhibit reduced CN
values of 4.30 and 3.75, respectively. This decrease is attributed to the
electrostatic interactions of -COO−group and LMS with Zn2+ ions,
which efﬁciently displace the coordinated water molecules around
Zn2+ ions and alter the solvation structures to [Zn(H2O)4(COO)]+ in PCZ
and [Zn(H2O)3(COO)LMS]+ in PLCZ. Additionally, the PLCZ polymer
electrolyte realizes rapid Zn2+ ion diffusion and intercalation with high
self-diffusion coefﬁcient (Ds) of 7.55 × 10−11 m2 s−1 (Fig. 1c and Supple-
mentary Fig. S5), due to the formed highly selective transportation
microchannels by -COO- within PAAS chain and LMS platelets. Fig-
ure 1d shows the digital photographs of the PLCZ electrolyte, which
exhibits a complete structure and no visible damages even after
kneading, highlighting its good ﬂexibility and restorability. The strain-
stress tests of the PLCZ with and without ZnSO4 immersion validate
that the Hofmeister effect of Zn2+ ion greatly improves the mechanical
properties of the PLCZ (Supplementary Figs. S6 and S7). The optimum
ratio of the components for the fabrication of the PLCZ electrolytes
was determined through galvanostatic cycling tests conducted on
Zn | |Zn symmetric cells. The P0.1L0.1CZ achieves a lower and ﬂatter

0.5 mA cm−2 when in comparison to CZ, PCZ and another PLCZ elec-
trolytes (Supplementary Fig. S8), meaning a reduced Zn deposition
barriers and high reversibility of Zn deposition/dissolution, which is
also proved by the Zn nucleation overpotential in Supplementary
Fig. S9. Scanning electron microscope (SEM) was employed to observe
the surface and internal structure of the PLCZ electrolyte. The PLCZ
electrolyte features a sleek and consistent surface (Fig. 1e) and a dense

SEM was carried out to compare the morphology of Zn electrodes
after different cycles (50, 100 and 200). As shown in Supplementary
Fig. S26 and Fig. 3c, d, distinct Zn protrusions with interposed cellulose
nanoﬁbers are observed on the surfaces of Zn electrodes when using
the CZ and PCZ. In stark contrast, the PLCZ electrolyte yields a uniform
and ﬂat surface morphology (Fig. 3e). Notably, the cross-sectional view
reveals intimate adhesion between the PLCZ polymer electrolyte and
Zn electrode, while signiﬁcant cavity and ravine are clear between the
PCZ and electrode due to pronounced Zn dendrite growth. This
observation indicates that the PLCZ is capable of establishing a robust
solid-electrolyte interface and facilitating limited volume expansion
toward Zn electrode36. These different Zn deposition/dissolution
behaviors of the electrolytes are further disclosed by confocal laser
scanning microscopy (CLSM), in which the PLCZ causes a more com-
pact surface with the reduced surface roughness of 1.6 (Supplemen-
tary Fig. S27). The surface morphology of the CZ, PCZ and PLCZ after
different cycles was also investigated (Supplementary Fig. S28).
Unwanted dendrite agglutination and penetration are generated on
the surface of the CZ and PCZ at the 100th and 200th cycles, which
would pierce them and eventually lead to the failure of batteries.
Surprisingly, the PLCZ electrolyte maintains a clean and undamaged
structure even after 200 cycles.
Chronoamperometry (CA) was utilized to obtain a comprehensive
understanding of Zn2+ deposition behavior (Fig. 3f). Both CZ and PCZ
electrolytes undergo a continuous increase in current density within
400 s, indicative of a persistent 2D diffusion and vertical Zn deposition
behavior. However, owing to the favorable migration paths created by
PAAS chains and LMS platelets, Zn2+ ions initially follows a 2D diffusion
process for the ﬁrst 100 s before transitioning to stable 3D spatial
accumulation, causing homogeneous Zn deposition. Tafel curves were
conducted to monitor the surface corrosion of Zn electrodes in the
electrolytes. Figure 3g demonstrates that the PLCZ polymer electrolyte
achieves a smaller corrosion current density (icorr) of 7.08 × 10−4A cm−2
than the CZ (5.89 × 10−3A cm-2) and PCZ (1.91 × 10−3A cm−2). This implies
that the PLCZ effectively mitigates the intractable corrosion issue of Zn
electrode. On account of the improved anti-corrosion and less free
water in the electrolyte, the PLCZ signiﬁcantly elevates the onset
potential of OER and HER at various temperatures, compared with the
CZ and PCZ (Supplementary Fig. S29). Consequently, symmetric cells
with the PLCZ electrolyte all deliver superior cycling stability over
4200 h at 273.15 K, 1600 h at 313.15 K and 400 h at 333.15 K (Supple-
mentary Fig. S30). These PLCZ-enabled symmetric cells exhibit
exceptionally long cycling lifespans at high current densities and areal
capacities across wide temperature range, surpassing previously
reported state-of-the-art (quasi-)solid-state electrolytes (Supplemen-
tary Fig. S31)7,11,36–52.
Formation and properties of medium-entropy alloy layer
The CE of Zn deposition/dissolution, a pivotal parameter evaluating
reversibility, was examined in Zn | |Cu asymmetric cells12. The high
stability and reversibility of Zn deposition/dissolution by the PLCZ are
evident through a steady CE of 99.7% over 2400 cycles (Fig. 4a and
Supplementary Fig. S32). In contrast, the CZ and PCZ systems experi-
ence rapid cycling deterioration after only 110 and 580 cycles,
respectively. The stability of the PLCZ cell is also demonstrated at
harsher cycling condition (Supplementary Fig. S33). The PLCZ polymer
electrolyte enhances key aspects of the electrochemical performance
of Zn anode by facilitating rapid Zn2+ transport, promoting uniform Zn
nucleation and delaying surface corrosion and side reactions. These
improvements contribute to the stable cycling performance in Zn | |Cu
cells. Cyclic voltammetry (CV) analyses of the asymmetric cells reveal
that the PLCZ reduces the nucleation overpotential to a mere 23 mV
while maintaining strong current density (Supplementary Fig. S34),
indicating its ability to optimize reaction kinetics for fast and uniform
Zn deposition and dissolution38. SEM images of Cu electrodes along-
side their digital photographs provide further evidences that after
cycling, the PLCZ results in a smooth and dendrite-free Zn deposition/
dissolution behavior, contrasting with the messy feature of the CZ and
PCZ electrolytes (Fig. 4b). To deepen understanding of the superior
stability of Zn | |Cu cells with the PLCZ, the surface chemical informa-
tion of Zn anodes after 10 cycles were probed by X-ray photoelectron
spectroscopy (XPS) spectra. Figure 4c illustrates the recorded Si 2p
and Mg 1 s XPS peaks detected on the Zn surface, with peaks at 100.5
and 1301.6 eV corresponding to ZnxSiy
53,54 and ZnxMgy
55,56, respectively.
As Ar+ etching time increases gradually, the XPS peaks of alloy com-
ponents of ZnxSiy and ZnxMg are preserved, while the emergence of
new peaks at 102.4 and 1303.8 eV, attributed to Si-O57 and Mg-O58
bonds in the LMS material, indicates an interfacial reduction reaction
between Zn anode and the PLCZ electrolyte, leading to the formation
of a Zn-Mg-Si MEA SEI during cycling. Energy-dispersive X-ray spec-
troscopy (EDS) mapping depict the uniform distribution of Zn, Mg and
Si elements, proving the existence of the Zn-Mg-Si SEI on the Zn sur-
face (Supplementary Fig. S35). X-ray absorption spectra (XAS) of Zn
anode after depositing different Zn capacities (1, 3 and 5 mAh cm−2)
were used to investigate the local structure and chemical environment
of Si and Mg atoms. The Si and Mg atoms in the Zn anodes show a
much higher oxidation state than their metallic foils due to the exis-
tence of Si-O and Mg-O bonds (Fig. 4d, e). With increasing deposited
Zn, their oxidation states gradually decrease compared with the case
of 1 mAh cm−2. This arises from the electron transfer from Zn to Si and
Mg atoms for the formation of metallic Si and Mg in the Zn-containing
alloy components. Distinct changes in the r-space curves of the Si
K-edge and Mg K-edge are observed as increasing deposited Zn, sig-
nifying the coordination variation of Si and Mg, which corroborates
the increased formation of ZnxSiy and ZnxMg components (Fig. 4f, g).
Figure 4h schematically represents the formation of the MEA layer
from the PLCZ electrolyte. Additionally, density functional theory
(DFT) calculations were conducted to assess the binding energy of
each component with Zn2+ ion as a reﬂection of their zincophilic
capacity. The calculated binding energies for H2O, Si, Mg, Zn3Si, MgZn
and SiZn3 are −0.5, −0.59, −0.66, −1.04, −1.77 and −2.65 eV (Fig. 4i),
respectively. These results indicate that the Zn-containing MEA layer
has higher chemical afﬁnity towards Zn2+ ions, conducive to the
homogeneous nucleation and Zn2+ deposition with a lower Zn
nucleation barrier.
It is widely recognized that inadequate SEI robustness fails to
accommodate the volume ﬂuctuations in repeated Zn deposition/
dissolution processes, resulting in the accumulation of Zn dendrite

Discussion
We present a multifunctional PLCZ polymer electrolyte with tailored
ion channels, effectively suppressing dendrite growth, electrode cor-
rosion and by-product generation. Owing to the constructed ionic
channels, the designed PLCZ electrolyte can motivate fast and uniform
Zn2+ ion transport, regulate ionic solvation structure and reduce free
water content. The experimental results and theoretical calculations
demonstrate that the in-situ formed robust MEA SEI with abundant
zincophilic alloy ingredients enables a 3D spatial ion diffusion and
ensures a homogeneous Zn(002) deposition. Consequently, Zn | |Zn
cells of the PLCZ electrolyte can stably operate at various tempera-
tures, even at a deeper DOD of 85.6 % with current density of 2 mA cm−2
and areal capacity of 10 mAh cm−2. Furthermore, Zn | |Cu asymmetric
cells of the PLCZ electrolyte achieve an ultralong cycling over 2400
cycles with a high and stable average CE of 99.7 %. The PLCZ electrolyte
causes an improved Zn2+ reaction kinetics and discharge capacity to
Zn | |V2O5 full cells. Their assembled pouch cells with the industry-level
mass loading of 31.3 mg cm−2 obtains high discharge capacity of 1.13 Ah
and also show the potential for severe operating conditions such as
bending, shear damage and high temperatures. Overall, our electrolyte
design represents an innovative approach to high-performance and
stable Zn ion batteries.
Methods
Preparation of electrolytes
The PLCZ quasi-solid-state electrolyte was prepared by a sample ion-
exchange method. 30 g polymethyl cellulose nanoﬁber dispersion
(CNF, solid content ~2%) was added into 50 ml DI water. A certain
amount of PAAS (0.05 g, 0.1 g, 0.25 g and 0.5 g) was added into the
above solution and intensely stirred for 30 min, formed solution A. A
certain amount of LMS (0.05 g, 0.1 g, 0.25 g and 0.5 g) was dispersed in
50 ml DI water with stirring for 30 min, formed solution B. Then,
solution A and solution B were mixed together and stirred for 5 h. After
that, the resultant PAAS-LMS-CNF solution was poured into Teﬂon
petri dish and then dried at 348.15 K for 12 h. The formed polymer ﬁlm
is shown in Supplementary Fig. S3. Subsequently, the polymer ﬁlm was
ﬁrst soaked in DI water for 10 min and then immersed in 2 M ZnSO4
solution for 24 h. According to the used amount of PAAS and LMS, the
prepared quasi-solid-state electrolyte was marked as P0.05L0.05CZ,
P0.1L0.05CZ, P0.1L0.1CZ, P0.1L0.25CZ, P0.25L0.25CZ and P0.5L0.5CZ. The
optimal amounts of PAAS and LMS in solid-state solution were inves-
tigated through the galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) test of
symmetric cells at various current densities from 0.5 to 10 mA cm−2.
The CNF separator was prepared without any PAAS and LMS additives.
The batteries using CNF separator and 2 M ZnSO4 (120 μL) aqueous
solution was labelled as CZ. The PCZ quasi-solid-state electrolyte
containing 0.1 g of PAAS was also prepared.
Synthesis of V2O5 cathode material
10 g NH4VO3 was put into a crucible and heated at 673.15 K for 2 h with
ramping rate of 10 K min−1. After cooling down, the synthetic V2O5
powder was fully ground.
